Name: PyTorch
SDKs & notable repos: torchvision, torchaudio, torchtune, TorchServe; C++ and Python APIs
Downloadable / offline docs: Docs built per release and downloadable; source tree cloneable
Notes: The research default. `torch.compile` and the dispatcher are where the interesting engineering is — see also the PL/compilers index.

Name: TensorFlow
SDKs & notable repos: Keras, TFX, TF Lite / LiteRT, TensorFlow.js, TF Serving
Notes: Still dominant in some production and mobile settings. Google's devsite redirects automated clients to an auth page; loads fine in a browser.

Name: JAX
SDKs & notable repos: Flax, Optax, Haiku, Equinox; XLA backend
Notes: Composable transforms (`grad`, `jit`, `vmap`, `pmap`) over NumPy semantics. The cleanest mental model of autodiff in any framework.

Name: Keras
SDKs & notable repos: Backend-agnostic across TensorFlow, JAX and PyTorch since Keras 3

Name: scikit-learn
Notes: The user guide is a genuinely good free textbook on classical ML, not just API reference.

Name: XGBoost
SDKs & notable repos: Python, R, JVM, Julia; GPU training
Notes: Still the thing to beat on tabular data. Try it before any deep model on structured problems.

Name: fastai
Notes: The library and the course are designed together; use both or neither.

Name: Hugging Face
SDKs & notable repos: transformers, datasets, tokenizers, accelerate, peft, trl, diffusers
Downloadable / offline docs: All docs per library; models and datasets downloadable
Notes: The de facto model distribution layer for the field. The `transformers` source is also the best cross-architecture reference for how models are actually implemented.

Name: Transformers
SDKs & notable repos: Thousands of model implementations in a consistent structure
Notes: Read `modeling_llama.py` to see a modern decoder implemented plainly.

Name: OpenAI API
SDKs & notable repos: Python and Node SDKs; Agents SDK; Realtime API

Name: Anthropic / Claude API
SDKs & notable repos: Python, TypeScript SDKs; Agent SDK; MCP
Notes: The prompt-engineering and tool-use sections are unusually substantive.

Name: Google Gemini API
SDKs & notable repos: Python, JS, Go SDKs; Vertex AI for enterprise
Notes: Google devsite redirects bots to an auth page; fine in a browser.

Name: Mistral AI
SDKs & notable repos: Python and JS clients; open-weight models on Hugging Face

Name: Llama
Downloadable / offline docs: Docs site; weights downloadable under licence

Name: Ollama
SDKs & notable repos: Local model runner with an OpenAI-compatible API
Notes: The simplest way to run open-weight models locally.

Name: CUDA
Downloadable / offline docs: Programming Guide and Best Practices Guide as PDFs
Notes: The CUDA C++ Programming Guide is the foundational document for GPU performance work.

Name: Triton (OpenAI)
Notes: Write fused kernels without writing CUDA. The tutorials are the fastest route into GPU kernel thinking.

Name: TensorRT
SDKs & notable repos: Inference optimizer; TensorRT-LLM for language models

Name: OpenXLA / XLA
SDKs & notable repos: Compiler backend for JAX and TensorFlow; StableHLO
Notes: Read alongside MLIR — XLA is one of the best-documented production ML compilers.

Name: MLIR
SDKs & notable repos: Multi-level IR infrastructure underpinning most modern ML compilers
Notes: Part of LLVM. See the PL/compilers index for context.

Name: Apache TVM
SDKs & notable repos: Compiler stack targeting CPUs, GPUs and accelerators

Name: ONNX
Notes: Read the operator spec when debugging export problems — most issues are unsupported ops.

Name: DeepSpeed
Notes: The ZeRO papers and the matching code are the clearest explanation of memory-efficient distributed training.

Name: Megatron-LM
Notes: The reference implementation of tensor parallelism.

Name: Ray Train
SDKs & notable repos: Distributed training, tuning and serving on one substrate

Name: vLLM
Notes: The current default for serving open-weight LLMs. The PagedAttention design is worth reading as a systems idea.

Name: llama.cpp
SDKs & notable repos: GGML/GGUF; CPU and Metal inference; quantization
Notes: Readable C++ and the best practical education in quantization available.

Name: NVIDIA Triton Inference Server
Notes: Unrelated to OpenAI's Triton kernel language, despite the name.

Name: MLflow
Notes: Open-source and self-hostable, which matters more than it sounds.

Name: LangChain
SDKs & notable repos: Python and JS; LangGraph for stateful agents

Name: LlamaIndex
SDKs & notable repos: Retrieval and indexing over private data

Name: PEFT
Notes: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning is how most people actually adapt models. Read the LoRA docs before the paper.

Name: TRL
SDKs & notable repos: SFT, DPO, GRPO, PPO trainers for language models
Notes: Reference implementations of the alignment methods, readable and runnable.

Name: Unsloth
SDKs & notable repos: Memory- and speed-optimized fine-tuning with hand-written Triton kernels
Notes: The kernels are worth reading if you want to see Triton used for real work.

Name: Axolotl
SDKs & notable repos: Config-driven fine-tuning across many model families

Name: FlashAttention
SDKs & notable repos: IO-aware exact attention; now standard in nearly every training stack
Notes: The clearest demonstration that memory movement, not FLOPs, is the real constraint. Read the paper with the CUDA.

Name: SGLang
SDKs & notable repos: High-throughput LLM serving with RadixAttention prefix caching
Notes: The main alternative to vLLM. Comparing their scheduling designs is instructive.

Name: lm-evaluation-harness
SDKs & notable repos: The standard framework behind most published LLM benchmark numbers
Notes: If you want to know what a reported score actually measured, read the task definition here.

Name: FAISS
SDKs & notable repos: Similarity search and clustering of dense vectors; GPU support
Notes: The index-selection guide in the wiki is the practical reference for vector search.

Name: Sentence Transformers
SDKs & notable repos: Embedding and reranking models with a consistent API

Name: Gymnasium
SDKs & notable repos: The maintained successor to OpenAI Gym; the standard RL environment API

Name: CleanRL
SDKs & notable repos: Single-file implementations of RL algorithms with logged benchmark runs
Notes: Every algorithm in one readable file, with reproduced results. The best way to actually understand an RL algorithm.

Name: Stable-Baselines3
SDKs & notable repos: Reliable reference RL implementations in PyTorch

Name: Optax
SDKs & notable repos: Composable gradient transformations and optimizers for JAX
Notes: Reading Optax is the clearest way to understand what an optimizer actually does.

Name: Mojo
SDKs & notable repos: Python-superset language targeting ML hardware via MLIR
Notes: Early, and genuinely interesting as a language-design attempt. See the PL/compilers index for the MLIR context.

Name: arXiv
SDKs & notable repos: Preprints across all of CS; most systems, ML and PL work appears here before publication
Downloadable / offline docs: Every paper is a free PDF. Bulk access documented at https://info.arxiv.org/help/bulk_data/index.html; a full-text API at export.arxiv.org
Notes: Not peer-reviewed. Treat an arXiv-only paper as a claim, not a result — but it is where you will read almost everything first.

Name: ar5iv
SDKs & notable repos: Renders any arXiv paper as responsive HTML instead of PDF
Notes: Makes papers readable on a phone and searchable in-page. Underused.

Name: alphaXiv
SDKs & notable repos: arXiv papers with a public comment and discussion layer
Notes: Useful when a paper is contested — the discussion often contains the critique you were looking for.

Name: Semantic Scholar
SDKs & notable repos: 200M+ papers with citation graph, influential-citation scoring and TLDR summaries
Downloadable / offline docs: Free Graph API (https://www.semanticscholar.org/product/api), bulk datasets available on request
Notes: The best free citation graph. 'Highly influential citations' is a genuinely useful filter for finding what actually mattered.

Name: OpenAlex
SDKs & notable repos: Fully open catalogue of works, authors, venues and institutions; successor to Microsoft Academic Graph
Downloadable / offline docs: Entirely free API with no key required; complete database snapshots downloadable
Notes: The only large-scale bibliographic database that is open all the way down, including bulk snapshots.

Name: DBLP
SDKs & notable repos: Authoritative CS bibliography — complete author and venue listings
Notes: The fastest way to find everything a given researcher has published, and to see a conference's full programme by year.

Name: OpenReview
SDKs & notable repos: ICLR, NeurIPS, COLM and dozens of other venues — papers plus the full review threads
Notes: Reading the reviews and author rebuttals teaches you how the field evaluates work. Nothing else exposes this.

Name: CORE
SDKs & notable repos: Aggregates 300M+ open-access papers from repositories worldwide
Notes: Good for finding the green open-access copy when a publisher's version is paywalled.

Name: Unpaywall
SDKs & notable repos: Finds legal free copies of paywalled papers via DOI
Notes: Legal, author-deposited copies only. Install the extension and most paywalls simply stop appearing.

Name: Papers We Love
SDKs & notable repos: A curated, categorised repository of classic CS papers with local meetup talks
Downloadable / offline docs: Repo cloneable; many PDFs mirrored in-repo
Notes: The best starting point if you do not yet know which papers matter in a subfield.

Name: The Morning Paper (archive)
Notes: No longer updated, but the back catalogue of ~1000 summarised papers is one of the great free CS resources.

Name: USENIX Proceedings
SDKs & notable repos: OSDI, SOSP (co-published), NSDI, ATC, FAST, Security — the core systems venues
Downloadable / offline docs: Every paper free, immediately, with no membership. Often with recorded talks
Notes: USENIX made everything open access years before the rest of the field. If a systems paper exists, check here first.

Name: ACM Digital Library
SDKs & notable repos: SIGMOD, ASPLOS, PLDI, POPL, SoCC and the ACM journals
Downloadable / offline docs: Partly open: ACM Open and author-paid OA papers are free; others are paywalled
Notes: 403s to automated clients; loads in a browser. For paywalled items, check arXiv, the author's homepage or Unpaywall first — the free copy usually exists.

Name: IEEE Xplore
SDKs & notable repos: ISCA, MICRO, HPCA and the IEEE journals
Notes: Almost always worth searching the author's page or arXiv instead. Architecture authors in particular post preprints widely.

Name: DROPS / LIPIcs (Dagstuhl)
SDKs & notable repos: ECOOP, ITP, CONCUR, SAT and many theory venues
Downloadable / offline docs: 100% open access, free PDFs, Creative Commons licensed
Notes: A fully open publisher. Every paper, always free, no exceptions.

Name: arXiv cs.LG / cs.CL / cs.CV
SDKs & notable repos: Machine learning, computational linguistics and computer vision. See also https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CL/recent, https://arxiv.org/list/cs.CV/recent and https://arxiv.org/list/stat.ML/recent
Notes: Volume is overwhelming — hundreds of papers daily. Use curation (Hugging Face Papers, alphaXiv, Lil'Log) rather than reading the firehose.

Name: Papers with Code
SDKs & notable repos: Papers linked to implementations, with benchmark leaderboards by task
Downloadable / offline docs: Free; datasets and results available in bulk
Notes: The leaderboards are useful for orientation but gameable — check whether the comparison is fair before believing a ranking.

Name: Hugging Face Papers
SDKs & notable repos: Daily curated arXiv selection with community discussion and linked model weights
Notes: The most practical daily filter on the arXiv firehose, because papers are linked to runnable artifacts.

Name: NeurIPS Proceedings
Downloadable / offline docs: All free PDFs, plus supplementary material
Notes: Fully open archive going back nearly four decades.

Name: PMLR
SDKs & notable repos: Proceedings of Machine Learning Research — ICML, AISTATS, CoLLAs, UAI and more
Notes: If it was published at ICML, it is free here. No exceptions.

Name: JMLR
Notes: Longer, more rigorous papers than the conference venues. Founded specifically as an open-access protest.

Name: ACL Anthology
SDKs & notable repos: Every NLP paper from ACL, EMNLP, NAACL, COLING and more — 100,000+ papers
Downloadable / offline docs: All free; full BibTeX and metadata dumps in the repo
Notes: The model open-access archive. Complete, searchable, and permanently free.

Name: CVF Open Access
SDKs & notable repos: CVPR, ICCV, WACV papers in full
Notes: The entire computer vision conference output, openly hosted.

Name: OpenReview
SDKs & notable repos: ICLR, NeurIPS and others with full review threads
Notes: Read the reviews. For contested papers this is more informative than the paper.

Name: MLCommons / MLPerf
SDKs & notable repos: Standardised training and inference benchmarks with audited submissions
Notes: The only ML performance numbers with a credible verification process behind them.

Name: Google Research publications
SDKs & notable repos: Transformers, BERT, TPU architecture, MapReduce, Spanner
Notes: Search here before arXiv for anything Google-originated.

Name: Microsoft Research publications
SDKs & notable repos: DeepSpeed, ZeRO, Phi models, systems and PL work

Name: Lil'Log
SDKs & notable repos: Long-form technical surveys of research areas
Notes: Usually the best single explainer on a topic, with full citations. Start here before the primary papers.

Name: Distill
SDKs & notable repos: Interactive visual explanations of ML concepts
Notes: No longer publishing, but the back catalogue remains the high-water mark for explaining ML visually.

Name: Neural Networks: Zero to Hero (Karpathy)
Notes: Build backpropagation, then a language model, then GPT — on video, in order, from nothing. The best free introduction to deep learning that exists.

Name: micrograd
Notes: An autograd engine in roughly 100 lines. Read every line; autodiff stops being magic.

Name: nanoGPT
Notes: A GPT you can train yourself and actually read. ~300 lines of model code.

Name: nn-zero-to-hero repo
Notes: The notebooks accompanying the video series.

Name: fast.ai Practical Deep Learning
Notes: Top-down: get working models first, derive theory later. Free, and effective for people who learn by doing.

Name: Stanford CS231n
Notes: Computer vision and CNNs. Notes and assignments public; the notes remain among the clearest written.

Name: Stanford CS224n
Notes: NLP with deep learning. Slides and assignments public.

Name: Stanford CS229
Notes: Classical machine learning done properly. The lecture notes are a standalone reference.

Name: MIT Introduction to Deep Learning
Notes: A compact bootcamp with all lectures and labs free.

Name: Hugging Face courses
Notes: Free courses on NLP, diffusion, RL, audio and agents, each with runnable notebooks.

Name: Dive into Deep Learning (d2l.ai)
Notes: Interactive book with runnable code in PyTorch, TensorFlow and JAX. Used as a textbook at 500+ universities.

Name: Deep Learning (Goodfellow et al.)
Notes: Free online. The theory reference, though now dated on architectures.

Name: Probabilistic Machine Learning (Murphy)
Notes: Free PDFs. The modern successor to the classical statistical ML texts.

Name: scikit-learn user guide
Notes: A free textbook on classical ML hiding inside API documentation.

Name: PyTorch tutorials
Notes: Start with the 60-minute blitz, then the training loop from scratch.

Name: PyTorch docs
Notes: Learn to read these rather than searching for examples.

Name: scikit-learn
Notes: Do not skip classical ML. Most real problems are still tabular.

Name: XGBoost
Notes: On structured data this is still frequently the right answer.

Name: Hugging Face Transformers
Notes: The practical path to using pretrained models.

Name: Ollama
Notes: Run open-weight models on your own machine in one command.

Name: Papers We Love
Notes: Start here when you do not yet know which papers matter. Curated by subfield, with recorded talks.

Name: The Morning Paper archive
Notes: Around a thousand papers summarised in plain language. No longer updated; still one of the best free CS resources.

Name: Semantic Scholar
Notes: Free citation graph. The 'highly influential citations' filter is the fastest way to find what a paper actually changed.

Name: Unpaywall
Notes: Install the extension. Most paywalls stop appearing, legally, because the author deposited a copy.

Name: ar5iv
Notes: Read any arXiv paper as HTML instead of a two-column PDF. Swap arxiv.org/abs for ar5iv.labs.arxiv.org/html.

Name: Stanford CS336 — Language Modeling from Scratch
Notes: Build a language model end to end: tokenizer, architecture, training, systems, alignment. The most relevant advanced course currently public.

Name: Stanford CS224n
Notes: Later lectures cover current architectures and training practice.

Name: Stanford CS231n
Notes: Assignment 3 and the notes on optimization remain worthwhile.

Name: OpenAI Spinning Up in Deep RL
Notes: The best-structured free entry into reinforcement learning, with clean reference implementations.

Name: Probabilistic Machine Learning
Notes: For the theory under modern methods, including the advanced volume.

Name: Transformers source
Notes: Every major architecture in one consistent structure. Unmatched as a comparative reference.

Name: nanoGPT
Notes: Return to it after reading production code; the minimal version clarifies the essentials.

Name: Diffusers
Notes: Schedulers and pipelines for diffusion models, readable.

Name: llama.cpp
Notes: Quantization, GGUF, and CPU inference — a systems education in C++.

Name: vLLM
Notes: PagedAttention and continuous batching; a genuinely novel systems contribution.

Name: Triton tutorials
Notes: Write fused GPU kernels in Python. Work through the matmul and attention tutorials.

Name: CUDA Programming Guide
Notes: The memory hierarchy and occupancy chapters determine most real performance.

Name: CUDA samples
Notes: Reference kernels to compare your own against.

Name: cuDNN docs
Notes: What the primitives underneath your framework actually do.

Name: TensorRT
Notes: Inference-side graph optimization and precision calibration.

Name: OpenXLA / XLA
Notes: Operator fusion and layout assignment, documented properly.

Name: MLIR
Notes: The dialect infrastructure under most modern ML compilers. Also read the PL/compilers index.

Name: Apache TVM
Notes: Autotuning and codegen for heterogeneous targets.

Name: ONNX operator spec
Notes: Read the spec when export breaks — it usually will.

Name: ONNX Runtime
Notes: Execution providers and graph optimizations.

Name: DeepSpeed
Notes: ZeRO stages 1-3 and offloading, with papers alongside the code.

Name: Megatron-LM
Notes: Tensor and pipeline parallelism, reference implementation.

Name: PyTorch distributed docs
Notes: FSDP, DDP and the collective primitives underneath.

Name: Ray Train
Notes: Orchestration across the cluster; see the distributed-systems index too.

Name: JAX
Notes: `pmap`, `shard_map` and explicit sharding give the clearest model of parallelism in any framework.

Name: arXiv cs.LG
Notes: Where the field publishes first. Unfiltered, so pair with curation.

Name: Papers with Code
Notes: Papers linked to implementations and benchmark tables.

Name: Lil'Log (Lilian Weng)
Notes: Long-form technical surveys; usually the best single explainer on a new topic.

Name: Distill.pub
Notes: Archived but still the high-water mark for visual explanation of ML concepts.

Name: NeurIPS
Notes: Proceedings free.

Name: ICML
Notes: Proceedings free.

Name: ICLR
Notes: Reviews are public on OpenReview — reading them teaches you how the field evaluates work.
